_meta._note: Sept 16 falls in the afterfeast of the Elevation of the Holy Cross (Sep 14–21). The Sergius rubric prescribes two interleaved canons: Canon I of the feast (Cross, Tone VIII, by Cosmas of Maiuma) + Canon II of the holy great-martyr Euphemia (Tone VIII, by John the Monk). Cross/afterfeast content belongs to the Sep 14 feast and is handled by the assembler separately. This file authors St Euphemia's content only: single canon (Tone VIII), sessional hymn after Ode 3, Kontakion + Ikos, exapostilarion, and lauds (4 stichera + Glory + Both now). No Polyeleos, no Magnification. Great Doxology sung.

troparion.text:
Thy ewe-lamb Euphemia O Jesus, crieth out with a loud voice:
"Thee do I love, O my Bridegroom,
and, seeking Thee, I endure suffering.
In Thy baptism I am crucified and buried with Thee.
I suffer for Thy sake, that I may reign with Thee;
I die for Thee, that I may live with Thee.
Accept me, who with love sacrifice myself for Thee,
as an unblemished offering!"
By her supplications, in that Thou art merciful,//
save Thou our souls.
troparion.label: Troparion of the holy great-martyr Euphemia

kontakion.text:
Thou didst struggle well in thy contest,
and after death dost sanctify us with streams of miracles, O all-praised one.
Wherefore, we hymn thy holy repose,
having recourse to thy divine temple with faith,
that we may be delivered from spiritual afflictions,//
and draw forth the grace of miracles.
kontakion.label: Kontakion of the holy great-martyr Euphemia
kontakion.melody: Having been lifted up on the Cross

_meta._note: Two canons in the actual service: Canon of the feast (Cross afterfeast, Tone VIII) + Canon of St Euphemia (Tone VIII). Cross canon content omitted here per menaion-matins-track pattern; assembler injects afterfeast canon. Sessional hymns after Kathisma 1 and 2 are of the Cross afterfeast (handled by assembler). troparion._note: On 'God is the Lord': Troparion of the feast (Twice); Glory ..., Troparion of the holy great-martyr (Tone IV); Both now ..., of the feast (Once).

canon._author: Canon of the holy great-martyr Euphemia, the acrostic whereof is 'I praise the all-famed maiden', by John the Monk in Tone VIII. Canon of the feast (Cross afterfeast, Tone VIII) interleaved in the actual service is omitted per the menaion-matins-track pattern.

ode1.irmos:
Let us sing unto the Lord,
who led His people through the Red Sea://
for He alone hath gloriously been glorified.

troparia.text: By her miracles the most praised maiden hath drawn the armies of heavenly beings and the choirs of mortals to her hymnody.
Having spurned heritage and the splendor which cometh from wealth, the honored Euphemia acquired Christ in their place.
The Master of all, desiring the beauty of thy most comely heart, O all-praised one, hath deemed thee worthy of the mansions of heaven.
Theotokion: O most pure Theotokos, we hymn thee who supra-naturally gave birth to the incarnate, eternal and supremely divine Word.

ode3.irmos:
O Lord, thou art the confirmation of those who flee to Thee,
Thou art the Light of those in darkness,//
and my spirit doth hymn Thee.

troparia.text: Thou didst appear before the tribunal, bearing thy soul manfully, thereby vanquishing the cowardly enemy, O all-praised one.
There was neither blemish in thy beauty nor wrinkle in thy soul; wherefore Christ received thee as His bride in the bridal-chambers of incorruption.
Heal thou the wounds of my soul, O all-praised martyr of Christ, and by thy supplications calm the tempest of my life.
Theotokion: Thee have we Christians acquired as our refuge and bulwark, and thee do we glorify without ceasing, O unwedded bride.

sessionalHymnAfterOde3.text:
With the streams of thy blood O all-praised martyr of Christ,
thou dost ever drown the ungodly,
ever watering the noetic meadows with the gentle showers of grace,
and producing the grain of faith therein.
Wherefore, even after thy repose thou hast most gloriously been revealed to be a cloud pouring forth a witness to Life.
O all-praised passion-bearer, entreat Christ God,
that He grant remission of sins unto those who honor thy holy memory with love.
sessionalHymnAfterOde3.label: Sessional Hymn of the holy great-martyr (after Ode 3)
sessionalHymnAfterOde3._note: Sung twice. Glory ..., Both now ..., Sessional Hymn of the feast (Tone VIII).

bothNow.label: Both now ..., of the feast

troparia.text: Having made thyself an undistorted reflection of divine understandings, O martyr, thou didst shine forth as an exceedingly magnificent beacon among spiritual athletes.
Thou didst not offer sacrifices to the dark demon, O invincible martyr, for thou didst long to receive a life-bearing death for thy piety.
Bearing a body without pain, with the passion-bearers O immaculate one, thou didst remain insensible to thy wounds through divine love.
As thy countenance suffered patiently, O martyr, it was splendidly adorned with wounds and darkened the thoughts of the enemy with the lightning of the divine Spirit.
Theotokion: As Thou art sinless, O God, grant us purification from our ignorance, and grant peace to the world through the supplications of her who gave birth to Thee.
Recognizing that which is opposed to the day and to peace, thou didst not wish to embrace the war-loving demon.
Thinking to weaken thy divine strength, O martyr, the all-evil one was revealed to be daring in his wiles.
Grant me enlightenment and peace, O all-praised one, quelling my greatly vexing turmoil by thy prayers.
Theotokion: O Theotokos, we hymn thee who art a Virgin even after giving birth; for thou hast given birth to God the Word on behalf of all the world.

ode6.irmos:
O Thou that puttest on light as a garment,
grant me also a robe of light,//
O All-merciful Christ, our God.

troparia.text: Bearing manly wisdom of soul in thy womanly nature, O glorious one, thou didst pay no heed to the beasts in the waters.
Without sustaining harm, thou didst vanquish the pride of the tyrants in the waters, O invincible martyr, abiding with the beasts like Jonah.
Hearkening to thy supplications, the Lord delivered thee from the corruption of the beasts, as He did Daniel from the pit, O all-praised one.
Theotokion: O thou who at the word of the archangel hast given birth to the Word in the flesh, we pray thee to deliver our souls from the snares of the enemy.

kontakion.melody: Having been lifted up on the Cross

ikos.text: The temple of the all-praised one hath been shown to be a paradise, having in its midst a garden of immortality, her precious body; and those who gather the goodly flourishing fruits thereof are quickly sanctified. For beholding a dead body shedding blood like one that is alive, and perfuming all, they are awestruck. Wherefore, hasten ye, and with me the lowly one, let us be purified from all defilement; and, venerating it, let us draw forth the grace of miracles.

ode7.irmos:
The Children of Judaea, who of old came to dwell in Babylon,
trampled underfoot the flame of the furnace through their faith in the Trinity,
as they sang: 'O God of our fathers, blessed art Thou.'

troparia.text: The goodly courage of the divine martyr was shown to be beyond understanding; for the Creator of all causeth creation to submit to those who cry out amid sufferings: O God of our fathers, blessed art Thou!

The maiden closed the frivolous and prating mouths of the tyrants, and put down the pride of the all-iniquitous ones through the divine Spirit, chanting in a godly fashion: O God of our fathers, blessed art Thou!

Of old, the furnace having been set afire, was consumed by the three venerable youths, and now the divinely wise one, hymning the Trinity, hath ensnared the servants, hymning the God of our fathers: Blessed art Thou, O God!

The Bridegroom, mystically coming to His most pure bride in the furnace, hath by the dew of the Spirit, and at the behest of the Father, preserved her as she sang: O God of our fathers, blessed art Thou!

Theotokion: As Thou didst desire to arrange our salvation, O Savior, Thou didst make Thine abode within the Virgin's womb, and hast shown her to be the intercessor for the world. O God of our fathers, blessed art Thou!

ode8.irmos:
The King of heaven,
Who is glorified by the hosts of angels,
let us praise and supremely exalt throughout all ages.

troparia.text: The most blessed among women, having won the grace of the Most High as her reward, hymneth Christ, praising Him for all ages.
Fortified by the thought of her Bridegroom and by immaterial love, the martyr gave her body over to death, and liveth for all ages.
Having armed herself with the Holy Spirit against falsehood as against a wild beast, the martyr hath received her reward for all ages.
Thou didst not receive the death which corrupteth the soul, O pure and immaculate one, but by the bite of the wild beast didst right boldly exchange it for life which never waxeth old.
Theotokion: Thou dost fend off the assaults of temptations and the attacks of the passions, O Virgin; wherefore, we hymn thee throughout all ages.

ode9.irmos:
O Theotokos, thou art a mystical Paradise,
who untilled brought forth Christ,
by Whom the life-giving Tree of the Cross hath been planted upon the earth:
Therefore celebrating its exaltation on this day,
Him do we worship//
and thee do we magnify.

troparia.text: The flow of thy life's blood, O all-praised martyr, is a token of the incorrupt life given thee; for thou hast been revealed to be a treasury continually full of healings for those who draw forth from it with faith.

Death touched thee through the law of nature, O divinely wise one, for having dispassionately arrayed thyself in life-bearing mortality, and having laid down thy most honored and animate body, thou dost ever abide incorruptibly, of which the streams of thy blood bear witness to.

Crowned with the laws of suffering, O martyr Euphemia, thou preacher of Christ, the scroll of the pious and precious dogmas entrusted to thee by the council didst thou show forth, holding it in thy hands like a living pillar of Orthodoxy.

Theotokion: O Virgin Mother, thou Bride who knewest not wedlock, vessel of sweet fragrance, we magnify thee as the true and immaculate cloud of divine light who received the Rain of heaven in thy womb.

exapostilarion.text:
Having endured death for the living God, thou remainest alive, O all-praised Euphemia;
and holding in thy grasp His scroll,
thou wast a bulwark of defense for the Orthodox
who celebrate thine honored, divine and most sacred memory with faith.
exapostilarion.label: Exapostilarion of the holy great-martyr
exapostilarion._note: Sung twice. Glory ..., Both now ..., Exapostilarion of the feast.

bothNow.text:
With splendors of bright radiance and divine desire the Cross of the Lord, which lieth before us, doth summon all to its elevation.
Come ye all, and with joy, love and fear let us kiss it with faith
and glorify the one Creator and Master!
bothNow.label: Both now ..., of the feast

lauds._note: 4 Stichera of the holy great-martyr in Tone III; Glory in Tone VI (of the martyr); Both now in Tone VI (of the feast).

stichera.text: Beholding the spiritual athlete's victory accomplished with divine wisdom for the sake of our God, Who is wondrous in His counsels, O ye faithful, let us chant hymnody of thanksgiving; for in her womanly nature the goodly martyr vanquished the invisible might of the power of the adversary, perfecting her godly power in weakness. Through her supplications, save Thou our souls.

Beholding the spiritual athlete's victory accomplished with divine wisdom for the sake of our God, Who is wondrous in His counsels, O ye faithful, let us chant hymnody of thanksgiving; for in her womanly nature the goodly martyr vanquished the invisible might of the power of the adversary, perfecting her godly power in weakness. Through her supplications, save Thou our souls.
stichera._note: Repeated per the Sergius rubric: sung twice.

stichera.text: Mingling the cup of truth with the blood of her martyrdom, and ever offering it to the Church, with the voice of wisdom the most praised martyr of Christ summoneth the children of the Church therein, saying: "Draw forth the drink which beareth witness to the resurrection, which driveth away unbelievers, washing away the passions and preserving the souls of the pious who cry out to the Savior: O Thou Who hast given us to drink of the torrent of the Spirit's sweetness, save Thou our souls!"

O ye whose souls have been sealed with the blood of Christ unto the day of deliverance, with gladness of spirit let us draw forth, as the prophet saith, the holy blood which floweth forth for us from the well-spring of the martyr, as a token of the life-bearing sufferings of the Savior and everlasting glory. And let us cry aloud to Him: O Lord Who art glorious in Thy saints, through the supplications of Thine all-praised passion-bearer, save our souls!

doxastikon.text:
At the right hand of the Savior stood the virgin, passion-bearer and martyr Euphemia,
arrayed in the virtues, invincible,
adorned with the oil of purity and the blood of martyrdom;
and she crieth out to Him, joyfully holding a lamp in her hand:
"I have hastened to the sweet fragrance of Thy myrrh, O Christ God,
for I have been wounded with love of Thee!
Depart not from me, O my heavenly Bridegroom!"
By her supplications send down Thy mercies upon us,//
O almighty Savior.
doxastikon.label: Glory ..., of the holy great-martyr

theotokion.text:
Today the Cross of the Lord cometh forth;
and the faithful receive it with desire,
and they derive healings of soul and body, and every pang.
Let us venerate it with joy and fear:
with fear, for we are unworthy because of our sins;
and with joy, because of the salvation which is granted to the world by Christ God,
Who hath great mercy,//
and Who was nailed to it.
theotokion.label: Both now ..., of the feast
